preconditions.description: The input must contain exactly two integers n (number of cities) and m (number of citizens) where 2 ≤ n ≤ 20000 and 1 ≤ m ≤ 10000.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdin.split()[2:2 + n - 1])
preconditions.description: The next n-1 lines must describe the roads, each with two integers v and u (1 ≤ v, u ≤ n, v ≠ u) representing bidirectional roads.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.split()) == 2 + n - 1 + 2 * m and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdin.split()[2 + n - 1:])
preconditions.description: The next m lines must describe the citizens, each with two integers xi and yi (1 ≤ xi, yi ≤ n, xi ≠ yi) representing their home and work cities.

postconditions.description: The first line of output must be a single integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ n) representing the minimum number of puppies needed.

postconditions.expression: q == int(stdout.split()[1]) and all(1 <= int(a) <= m for a in stdout.split()[2:2 + q]) and len(set(stdout.split()[2:2 + q])) == q
postconditions.description: The second line must start with q (number of puppies given to citizens) followed by q distinct integers representing the indices of citizens to give puppies to.

postconditions.expression: e == int(stdout.split()[q + 2]) and all(1 <= int(b) <= n - 1 for b in stdout.split()[q + 3:q + 3 + e]) and len(set(stdout.split()[q + 3:q + 3 + e])) == e
postconditions.description: The third line must start with e (number of puppies given to guardians) followed by e distinct integers representing the indices of roads (guardians) to give puppies to.
The sum of q and e must equal k.

postconditions.expression: all(citizen_happy(citizen, roads, guardians_with_puppies, citizens_with_puppies) for citizen in citizens)
postconditions.description: Every citizen must be happy after the distribution of puppies, where a citizen is happy if either they have a puppy or all guardians along their path have puppies.
